chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Jamīl ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Samāʿah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding a man whom the Imam had preceded by one rakʿah, then the Imam erred and performed five; he said: “He makes up that rakʿah and does not take the Imam’s mistake into account.”

key_terms.أَوْهَمَ: made an error or became mistaken in the prayer
key_terms.الرَّكْعَةَ: the prayer unit that was missed
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the prayer leader in congregational salat
key_terms.بِرَكْعَةٍ: by one rakʿah; one unit of the prayer
key_terms.خَمْسًا: five rakʿahs, meaning an extra unit beyond the prescribed number
key_terms.لَا يَعْتَدُّ: he does not count or consider as valid for his own calculation
key_terms.يَقْضِي: he makes up or completes what he missed

ai.seo_question: What should a latecomer in congregational prayer do if the Imam mistakenly prays five rakʿahs?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one praying behind an Imam after having missed one rakʿah. If the Imam mistakenly prays five rakʿahs, the follower completes the missed rakʿah and does not treat the Imam’s mistaken extra rakʿah as counting for himself.
